sections.h2: Where is Northglenn and what kind of city is it?
sections.html:
Northglenn is a home rule city north of Denver that lies in both Adams and Weld counties and belongs to the Denver-Aurora-Lakewood metropolitan area. It covers about 7.4 square miles at an elevation near 5,364 feet.

Interstate 25, State Highway 7, State Highway 128 and the E-470 toll corridor all serve the area. ZIP codes include 80233, 80234, 80241 and 80260.

Unlike older Front Range towns, Northglenn did not grow around a railroad or a farm. It was built as a master planned community starting in 1959 by developer Jordon Perlmutter, and the city incorporated in 1969.

Population shows how quickly it filled in. The 1970 census counted 27,785 residents. The number slipped to 27,195 by 1990, then rose to 31,575 in 2000, 35,789 in 2010 and 38,131 in 2020. A city that reached nearly its current size within a decade of incorporation has a large stock of homes from the same era, and the earliest ones are now more than 60 years old.

For a seller, that history points to a few practical checks: the age of the roof and sewer line, the condition of original windows and any past additions that may not have been permitted.

sections.h2: How has Northglenn's population changed over time?
sections.html:
Northglenn's census counts show a city that filled in early and then held steady.

  • 1970: 27,785
  • 1980: 29,847
  • 1990: 27,195, a drop of 8.9 percent
  • 2000: 31,575
  • 2010: 35,789
  • 2020: 38,131

Because the city lost people in the 1980s and grew slowly afterward, much of its housing is probably original stock rather than newer construction. Sellers with homes from the first decades of the city often have original systems that a buyer will want to inspect, and an as-is sale can spare you from managing those repairs before closing.

sections.h2: What is the weather like and how does it affect a house in Northglenn?
sections.html:
Northglenn has a semi-arid climate. The hottest day on record reached 108 degrees Fahrenheit on August 2, 2008, and the coldest fell to minus 24 degrees on December 22, 1990.

That swing is about 132 degrees between extremes, and the structures that feel it most are roofs, gutters, exterior paint, heating systems and cooling equipment. Buyers who finance usually expect an inspection to flag them, which is one reason a cash sale appeals to owners who would rather not repair before closing.

sections.h2: How do commuters get around from Northglenn?
sections.html:
Transit is one of Northglenn's selling points. The city connects directly to Downtown Denver through the Regional Transportation District N Line at the Northglenn/112th station.

  • Interstate 25 and State Highways 7 and 128 are listed as the major highways serving the city.
  • The E-470 corridor also serves the area.
  • The N Line gives commuters a rail option into the downtown core.

A rail link into Downtown Denver is a feature a buyer can verify, so mention it when describing the house.

The 2020 census found 38,131 residents with a median age of 34.5. About 23 percent were under 18 and 12.6 percent were 65 or older. Of 13,954 households, 34.2 percent had children under 18, 41.7 percent were married-couple households, and 24.5 percent were one person living alone.

The Census reported that 36.8 percent of residents were Hispanic or Latino of any race.

The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.8 percent and the rental vacancy rate was 7.3 percent, so rental housing makes up a meaningful part of the city. That is useful if you are selling a house with a tenant in it.

sections.h2: When are property taxes due for a Northglenn home in Adams County?
sections.html:
Adams County lists a first-half payment due February 28, a second half due June 15 and a full payment due April 30. Only half or full payments are accepted, and partial payments are not. When the tax is $25 or less, the half-payment option does not apply and the full amount is due by April 30.

Tax notices go out in January, and the county explains that property taxes are collected one year in arrears. Delinquent notices are mailed in July, and unpaid real property taxes can be listed for the annual tax lien sale in the fall. Prepayments of next year's tax must arrive by noon on the last business day of December.

If you own the Weld County portion of Northglenn, the Weld County Treasurer bills that parcel instead. Confirm the county on your tax bill before you plan a payoff.

sections.h2: What does the Adams County tax calendar look like through the year?
sections.html:
Adams County publishes a month-by-month calendar that helps you see where a house stands before you sell.

  • January: tax notices are sent.
  • February: first-half payment due, by receipt or postmark on the 28th.
  • April: full payment due on the 30th.
  • June: second-half payment due on the 15th.
  • July: delinquent tax notices are mailed.
  • September: unpaid real property taxes are advertised ahead of the tax lien sale.
  • Late December: the Board of County Commissioners certifies the tax roll and sets the mill levy.

Colorado reappraises real property every two years, in odd-numbered years, according to Larimer County's explanation of the state cycle. A house in Northglenn is therefore revalued in odd years, and your valuation notice is the place to check what the assessor believes the house is worth.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed involve for a Northglenn sale?
sections.html:
A sale transfers title by a deed that is recorded with the county clerk and recorder. Weld County's recording guidance, which reflects Colorado law, says a document that transfers title for more than $500 carries a state documentary fee of 1 cent per $100, and every deed must include the buyer's mailing address.

  • Margins must be at least one inch top and bottom and half an inch left and right.
  • Recording fees are set by statute and must accompany the document.
  • Do not include Social Security numbers, because recorded documents are public.
  • Documents sent to the wrong county are not refunded, so confirm Adams or Weld first.

A title or closing company normally handles these steps in a cash sale, but the checklist helps you read the closing statement.

sections.h2: How should a Northglenn seller choose between listing and a cash sale?
sections.html:
A listing can reach more buyers, while a cash sale can close on a schedule you choose.

Tell us if the house has a tenant, a lien, an inherited title or deferred repairs. We will explain how each factor affects the process and what an as-is purchase would involve.

faqs.q: Is Northglenn in Adams County or Weld County?
faqs.a: Northglenn lies in both Adams and Weld counties. The county that holds your parcel bills the tax and records your deed.

faqs.q: When are Adams County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due February 28, the second half June 15 and a full payment April 30. Adams County does not accept partial payments.

faqs.q: How far is Northglenn from downtown Denver by transit?
faqs.a: The RTD N Line runs from the Northglenn/112th station to Downtown Denver. Check RTD for current schedules and trip times.
The 2020 census counted 38,131 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2024 estimate was 38,287.

faqs.q: What ZIP codes does Northglenn use?
faqs.a: Northglenn uses ZIP codes 80233, 80234, 80241 and 80260. Use the one on your tax bill when you give an address to a title company.

faqs.q: Do I pay a state fee when I sell a house in Colorado?
faqs.a: Colorado charges a documentary fee of 1 cent per $100 on transfers above $500. Your closing statement will show the exact amount.
